#| code-fold: false
best_cutoffs = cutoffs[error_rate == error_rate.min()]

No.
The curve in @fig-error-rate-curve is a staircase.
The [error rate](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/metrics.html#def-error-rate) changes only where $c$ crosses one of the
`r length(unique(py$ink_01))` values that the center ink takes,
and it is flat everywhere in between,
so its slope is 0 wherever the slope exists.
Gradient descent would never move.

The search found the lowest error rate,
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * min(py$error_rate))`%,
for every cutoff tried from `r sprintf("%.2f", min(py$best_cutoffs))` to `r sprintf("%.2f", max(py$best_cutoffs))`,
by trying each value in turn.
That works for one [parameter](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-parameter),
but trying every combination of values for a network with thousands of them is out of reach.

:::
